Well, I had a very strong team. I chose my former chief of staff, Beth Myers. She had served with me when I was governor of Massachusetts to lead the debate preparation effort. And she had teams of people delving into various issue areas and preparing briefing books for me. Because one of the things you're most concerned about is they'll raise a question you don't have an answer for. And you don't want to get up there and look foolish. And then we would have sessions where I would go back and forth with five or six members of my staff, and I would suggest a model answer, and they'd tell me what was wrong with it, and I'd try and incorporate their thoughts. And then finally, when you get ready for the presidential debates, we would actually rent a small ballroom at a hotel, set it up like a debate stage. And I would be debating someone. Rob Portman, Senator from Ohio, was by sparring partner. He was representing Barack Obama. And he and I would go back and forth. We'd have a moderator ask questions. We'd go back and forth and hit each other. Of course, he has all these notes ready. He's reading from a book and just beating that guy on me. It gets a little frightening when you think, oh boy, this could be tough. But that's the process. There aren't canned answers. I didn't have an answer for all the possible questions.
